headline: Anthropic faces test of its safety pledge as a public company
pages: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei rang the Nasdaq opening bell on Thursday and said an obsession with safety has been built into the company from the start. Anthropic raised a record $81.3 billion in its IPO and another $26 billion in a private placement, putting it among companies valued above $1 trillion. NPR reports that public ownership now tests the company's safety-first reputation. New investors, more scrutiny and pressure to deliver returns could complicate decisions that hurt the share price, such as delaying a risky model, legal experts said.

The IPO prospectus warns that sufficiently advanced AI could pose catastrophic or existential risks and admits there is no assurance its safeguards will be adequate. Why it matters: one of the most prominent AI developers must now balance its stated mission against shareholder expectations. Source: NPR.
